bullets.title: Tech calls cheap despite elevated skew — NVDA highlighted as upside play
bullets.body: Call skew percentiles are at +90th percentile while IV ranks are at <=7, meaning tech calls are historically cheap on an absolute basis. NVDA is specifically flagged as an attractive vehicle to express upside given this options market structure.

bullets.title: Meta's AI app Muse hits #1 on US Apple App Store
bullets.body: Meta's new AI app Muse reached the top-ranked free app position on the US Apple App Store, signaling strong early consumer traction for the product.

bullets.title: Micron India ramp: tens of millions of units in 2026, hundreds of millions in 2027
bullets.body: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra confirmed at SEMICON India 2026 that the Gujarat Surat packaging/test facility — India's first semiconductor facility under the country's chip program — began commercial production in 2026 and will scale to tens of millions of units this year and hundreds of millions in 2027.

bullets.title: CRWV and NBIS: framework for evaluating capital-intensive neo-cloud names
bullets.body: Commentary flags that CRWV and NBIS look very different from traditional software and require evaluation through CapEx, cash flow, balance sheets, growth trajectory, and associated risks — not conventional SaaS metrics.

bullets.title: Anthropic and OpenAI pivoting to smaller data center deals for faster capacity deployment
bullets.body: Both Anthropic and OpenAI are exploring smaller 20-30 MW data center deals in the US, UK, and Nordics, per CNBC sources. Smaller deals offer faster time to usable compute capacity compared to the hyperscale commitments they have pursued previously.

bullets.title: Tesla FSD shows 40% fewer collisions in Australia/New Zealand
bullets.body: Teslas operating on FSD (Supervised) in Australia and New Zealand experienced 40% fewer collisions on average versus non-FSD vehicles, adding data points to the autonomous safety narrative.

bullets.title: AI productivity boom thesis remains unproven — no disinflation, no white-collar job losses yet
bullets.body: Skeptical macro commentary notes that AI bulls expected a disinflationary productivity boom with negative employment impact on white-collar workers, but neither outcome has materialized. The Economist separately reports AI has created ~1 million new US jobs, complicating the displacement narrative.

bullets.title: AI bulls' opposition to rate hikes linked to personal exposure and thesis integrity
bullets.body: Commentary argues AI bulls oppose rate hikes partly because they personally benefit from the AI boom and because rate hikes risk revealing that AI's actual economic impact is weaker than the bullish consensus claims — creating an intellectual conflict of interest.

bullets.title: AI sector facing multiple headwinds: data center pushback, political scrutiny, rate hikes
bullets.body: A cluster of macro headwinds is pressuring AI infrastructure momentum: local community opposition to new data centers, growing voter and political concern about AI risks, and rate hikes creating cost-of-capital pressure on capital-intensive build-outs.

bullets.title: Semiconductor trajectory now central to S&P 500 earnings growth
bullets.body: Commentary flags that S&P 500 earnings growth is increasingly sensitive to semiconductor sector performance, noting 'we are all semis analysts now' — suggesting semis will be a critical swing factor for broader market earnings in coming years.

bullets.title: DXY hits highest since July, on pace for 8th straight day without a red close
bullets.body: The US Dollar Index reached its highest level since July and is tracking toward an 8th consecutive session without a closing decline — a notable streak suggesting sustained dollar strength against macro backdrop.

bullets.title: French-German 10Y spread widens to 100bps — highest since 2012
bullets.body: The French 10-year yield premium over German bunds hit 100 basis points, the widest spread since 2012, flagging elevated Eurozone fiscal and political stress. EU Economic Commissioner warns rising bond yields will affect all of Europe and calls for stronger fiscal discipline.

bullets.title: Bank of Japan hike disappoints on forward guidance; yen weakens sharply
bullets.body: The Bank of Japan raised rates 25bps to the highest level since 1995, but forward signaling on future hikes disappointed markets and the yen weakened following the announcement.

bullets.title: Diesel crisis deepens: US diesel at $6.45/gal record; Exxon Joliet refinery disruption
bullets.body: US diesel hit a fresh record of $6.45/gallon (AAA) while crude oil fell for a third consecutive day, widening the crack spread divergence. Separately, Exxon's Joliet refinery suffered a disruption threatening Midwest diesel supply, and US gas prices hit $4.43/gallon — the highest ever for this point in September.

bullets.title: Saudi Arabia cuts crude allocations to European refiners next month
bullets.body: Saudi Aramco has informed European oil refiners they will receive no crude in the coming month, a significant supply cut that compounds existing energy price pressures in Europe.

bullets.title: Warsh Fed likely to mirror hawkish market expectations, per analyst analogy
bullets.body: Commentary draws an analogy to the 2010s Fed being reluctant to disappoint dovish market expectations, suggesting the Warsh-led Fed may similarly be reluctant to disappoint the current hawkish consensus — implying higher-for-longer policy alignment.

bullets.title: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing solid but housing data disappoints sharply
bullets.body: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (ISM-adjusted) dipped to 58.3 in September but remains in expansion, with 68% of manufacturers expecting higher Q3 production. In contrast, August housing starts fell 2.6% MoM vs a +6.7% estimate, driven by a 22% MoM collapse in multifamily; pending home sales also moved further negative YoY.

bullets.title: AAII sentiment bull-bear spread at lowest since May 2025 for 9th straight week below average
bullets.body: The AAII bull-bear spread plunged to its lowest reading since May 2025 and has now remained below its historical average for nine consecutive weeks, suggesting broadly cautious retail sentiment.

bullets.title: Warren Buffett steps down as Berkshire Hathaway chairman, appointed Chairman Emeritus
bullets.body: Warren Buffett stepped down as chairman of Berkshire Hathaway effective immediately and was appointed Chairman Emeritus. No succession details on investment management disclosed in the announcement.

bullets.title: US markets to extend to 23-hour trading Mon-Fri starting December 6
bullets.body: US equity markets are set to begin trading 23 hours per day Monday through Friday starting December 6, with just a one-hour daily break for maintenance — a structural change that could affect liquidity dynamics and after-hours price discovery.
